name: CommerceML (1C, МойСклад)
description: Exchange with 1C:Enterprise and anything else that speaks CommerceML 2 — the catalogue and offers come in, orders go out. The shop decides which of its fields each 1C attribute fills, and nothing is created behind its back.

settings.label: Connection and matching
settings.help: The address to give 1C, what it has sent so far, and which of your price types, characteristics and statuses its own are. Matching is data, not a setting — it lives on its own screen.

options.create: Create new only, never touch existing
options.none: Nothing — receive and record, change nothing

settings.label: Products
settings.help: "Nothing" is the setting to start with: the first exchange then only fills the matching screen, and you see what 1C actually sends before it can write anything.

options.hidden: Hidden — reachable by link, absent from listings

settings.label: A product 1C has just created is
settings.help: Hidden by default on purpose: a product arrives from 1C with no photo, no description and no category of yours, and a shop should choose when that goes on sale.

settings.label: Create categories automatically
settings.help: Off means every new group waits on the matching screen instead. A catalogue tree is usually 1C's to own, so this is on.

settings.label: Create characteristics automatically
settings.help: Off by default, and deliberately the other way round from categories: 1C's properties are an internal bookkeeping vocabulary, and letting them into the shop unread is how a filter panel grows forty entries nobody meant to publish.

settings.label: Take prices and stock from offers.xml
settings.help: Off when the shop prices for itself and 1C is only the source of the catalogue.

settings.label: When 1C changes something it already sent

options.add: Add the new category, keep the others
options.new_only: Ignore — categories are set on the first import only

options.add: Add the new photo to the gallery
options.replace: Replace every photo the product has
options.new_only: Ignore — photos are set on the first import only

settings.label: Photographs
settings.help: "Ignore" is the default because "replace" destroys, every night, the photographs the shop took itself. Turn it up only when 1C is genuinely the better photographer.

settings.label: The first exchange, on a catalogue that already exists
Recognise a category by its name
settings.help: Only for rows that have no 1C identifier yet: matching by name once is how an existing catalogue acquires its links. Afterwards the identifier is what counts, and renaming either side changes nothing.

settings.label: Recognise a product by its article number
settings.help: Same rule, and the same one exchange conventions everywhere here follow: the identifier first, the shop's own key only when there is no identifier yet.

settings.label: Which 1C field fills which of ours
Fill these on the first import only
settings.help: What the shop edits after the import and does not want overwritten tonight. Names and descriptions are ticked because they are usually rewritten for the storefront the day a product arrives.

settings.label: Weight
settings.help: The names of the ЗначенияРеквизитов entries to read this from — one per line, and the last one actually present wins. This bag is open-ended and no two 1C configurations name it alike, which is why it is typed rather than guessed. Weight is read in kilograms and stored in whole grams.

settings.label: Length
settings.help: Read in centimetres, stored in whole millimetres.

settings.label: Products per request
settings.help: The protocol is built to be sliced: 1C asks again while the shop answers "progress". Lower this if the import times out; raising it does not make the whole exchange much faster.

settings.label: Largest chunk 1C may send, bytes
settings.help: Announced at the start of the exchange; 1C splits bigger files itself and the shop appends the pieces. Keep it under what PHP will accept in one request.

settings.label: Shipment is reported as
settings.help: The names of the attributes to read the shipment from — one per line, the last one present wins, exactly as for weight. A name that is present and not empty is the event; its value is only written to the log. What it moves the order to is chosen on the exchange screen.

settings.label: Payment is reported as
settings.help: Same rule. Payment is not a status here — it is the order's second axis — so this marks the order paid through the shop's own settlement, the one the manager's "mark as paid" runs. An order already paid is left alone.

permissions.name: commerceml.manage
permissions.label: Set up the 1C exchange and match its data
